note: Locks dot size as a TRUE DEVICE PIXEL quantity. `outputHeight` is pinned to the 1080-line authoring reference because the published clip size is dot_size / outputHeight -- unpinned, this digest would depend on the host. dot_size 12 at 1080 is 0.011111 clip, well clear of the 0.0035 the baked `transform.scale` gives, so a regression that fell back to the transform fails here rather than passing quietly; the fixture keeps `transform.scale` for exactly that reason. The grid wires follow the dots and now taper between their two endpoints' composed sizes, so this pins that contract too: at 12px the endpoints sit around 0.002 clip, above the 0.0006 floor. Paired with `particle-ripples-dots-4k`, which is the same case at twice the height and must produce half the clip size. Parity-checked by ParitySelfTests.testEffectScaleParity(), which digests the same clip formula.
